thread.title_full: Díaz-Balart votes to extend Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act through April 2029

author: Sunshine Sentinel
title: Díaz-Balart votes to extend Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act through April 2029
text:
Congressman Mario Díaz-Balart, Chairman of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs, announced on Apr. 29 that House Republicans voted to extend S.1318, the Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act, through April 2029.
The extension is intended to continue protections for American civil rights while maintaining national security measures against foreign threats. The act’s reauthorization follows previous reforms designed to increase oversight and safeguard privacy.
“In 2024, when House Republicans extended FISA at President Trump’s urging, we did so with the largest FBI and FISA reforms in decades. The reauthorization included 56 new civil rights reform mandates implemented to establish guardrails to protect Americans’ right to privacy. This FISA extension will continue to protect American civil rights and U.S. national security from hostile foreign threats,” Díaz-Balart said in a statement.
Since the law took effect in 2024, there has been a reduction in queries involving U.S.-persons. The legislation limits law enforcement’s ability to search Section 702 databases for evidence of crimes and restricts use of this information solely for foreign intelligence purposes. Currently only a small percentage of law enforcement personnel have access: just six percent can access FISA Section 702 data today, with only three percent of all such data accessed in 2025.
Section 702 is specifically intended for targeting individuals outside the United States who are considered threats; it cannot be used by the government to target Americans’ electronic communications without obtaining a warrant under other authorities.
Mario Díaz-Balart has served as Florida’s representative for its 26th District since 2003 after earlier terms in both chambers of Florida’s legislature according to his biography. He was born in Fort Lauderdale in 1961 and currently resides in Miami as reported by official congressional records. Díaz-Balart earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of South Florida according to university records.
